correctness.rationale: The exact fibre power is a scalar geometric series with factor sin(n theta)/sin theta; the positive 2x2 singular value is Phi. The shear with multiplier b/(2i sin theta) proves similarity; a uniform sine-orbit lower bound and two radial resolvent tests prove necessity for power and Kreiss. A Riemann–Lebesgue mixing argument on superlevel sets establishes the arbitrary-symbol norm limit. Blow-up rescalings theta=x/n and theta=epsilon x with tail bounds give every sharp power and resolvent coefficient. At alpha=1 the exact scalar maximum is sqrt(1+c^2/4), and at alpha>1 the diagonal resolvent dominates. Standard-library checker independently verifies matrix products and inverses in 7,519 finite assertions; the infinite proof does not rely on sampling.

value.rationale: A complete four-way criterion for arbitrary L-infinity couplings of opposite unitary multipliers, together with sharp power and resolvent phase diagrams for a natural vanishing-order family, is a structural operator-theory result. It gives every sublinear power exponent, the exact associated radial exponent and a nontrivial critical finite resolvent coefficient, separating Kreiss/power behaviour from an entire continuum of near-resonant failures. The theorem is motivated by current Foguel operator problems rather than a chosen isolated parameter.
